summary:
AEGIS is an astronaut health and cognitive-performance decision-support prototype designed to support crew well-being during long-duration space missions, particularly when communication with Earth is delayed or unavailable. The project focuses on fatigue, attention and cognitive performance by bringing together relevant spaceflight research, physiological context and performance indicators.

The prototype is designed to provide an overall crew overview, individual crew profiles, performance trends, potential alerts and a What-If simulation environment. It aims to help astronauts and mission support personnel understand changes in performance, review possible contributing factors and consider appropriate responses.

AEGIS addresses the challenge of maintaining astronaut health and performance in the demanding space environment, where microgravity, disrupted sleep patterns and mission conditions can affect human physiology and behaviour. By presenting research-informed information in an accessible mission-control interface, AEGIS aims to support better-informed, human-led decisions during future space exploration.
details:
AEGIS is designed as a human-in-the-loop decision-support prototype for astronaut health and cognitive performance during spaceflight. Its primary focus is fatigue, attention and cognitive performance, while also considering the wider physiological challenges associated with microgravity.

The prototype is organised around several key functions:

1. Mission Overview

Provides an overall view of the crew, mission conditions, communication status, performance indicators and potential alerts. This allows users to understand the general status of the crew from one interface.

2. Individual Crew Profiles

Provides individual crew information and performance trends. The intended system allows users to examine changes over time rather than relying on a single observation.

3. Alert and Evidence Review

Presents potential performance concerns together with supporting information, data quality and uncertainty. Rather than making medical diagnoses, AEGIS is intended to help users understand what has changed and why further attention may be needed.

4. What-If Simulation

Explores hypothetical mission situations, such as delayed observations, worsening reaction-time performance and communication interruptions. This allows users to consider how different circumstances could affect the availability and interpretation of crew information.

5. Scientific Research Integration

The project draws on NASA spaceflight research and relevant scientific literature to establish its research foundation. The team investigated datasets involving astronaut biological responses, neural organoids, skeletal muscle adaptation and cellular responses to microgravity. These studies provide scientific context for understanding spaceflight-related physiological changes.

The project considers the importance of distinguishing actual research measurements, published scientific findings, synthetic demonstration data and hypothetical simulation scenarios. These categories must not be treated as interchangeable.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AEGIS aims to:

  • Support awareness of astronaut fatigue, attention and cognitive-performance changes.
  • Present relevant information in a centralised and understandable interface.
  • Help astronauts and mission support personnel interpret potential performance concerns.
  • Provide a framework for considering microgravity-related physiological challenges.
  • Support human decision-making when communication with Earth is limited.
  • Encourage safer and more informed human spaceflight operations.

Tools and Technologies

The prototype was developed using Figma and Figma Make for interface design and interactive prototyping. Super Intelligence tools were used to support research, ideation, information organisation and visual development.

The current prototype is a concept and decision-support interface. It does not yet contain a fully implemented or scientifically validated AI/ML prediction engine, and its demonstration information must not be interpreted as real-time astronaut health monitoring.

Creativity and Innovation

AEGIS combines astronaut performance monitoring concepts, scientific research references and mission-scenario simulation in one interface. Its key innovation is the emphasis on explaining performance changes and presenting supporting evidence, rather than simply displaying health indicators or generating alerts without context.

The team considered the limitations of available spaceflight datasets, the distinction between laboratory experiments and actual astronaut measurements, data availability, uncertainty, communication delays and the importance of keeping humans involved in decision-making.
